coaching.headline: Willy's Belica owned the lobby. We leaked the middle objectives, then took Orb Prime and the whole damn base.
coaching.team: A proper win built on Belica's damage and Wukong's objective work. We took first blood and the first Fangtooth, then let the middle slip: they took the next two Fangtooths, and their Mini Prime fell with all five of us alive. After that Mini Prime they never took another major objective. Orb Prime led into an Inner Tower, the inhibitors and the core, and we finished ten structures to their one. The finish was clean; the middle was sloppy as hell.

focus.title: Answer every enemy objective
focus.action: When the enemy starts Fangtooth or Mini Prime and none of us is dead, one player calls contest or trade immediately and the team commits to it. Next game, count enemy majors that fall with all five alive and nothing taken back.

perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy put on a fucking clinic. Belica out-damaged everyone in the lobby by a mile, died once, and more than doubled his usual damage rate on the hero. Nothing there needs repair. The standard is the next layer: when her picks leave them a body down and a Fangtooth, Mini Prime or tower is reachable, Belica names it before hunting the next kill.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks did the grunt work that ends games: Wukong's objective damage beat the rest of our team combined, and his hero damage ran above his usual. The soft spot: he was dead both times they took Fangtooth, and a dead jungler at the pit is just an expensive farmer. When Fangtooth is about to spawn, Wukong calls the timer and the contest-or-trade choice before the next fight starts.
perPlayer.84d3231f-1ca1-4701-8d7f-c7133f7f03e9: Keep that shit. OasisTG07 made Murdock's night miserable, kept deleting Greystone, and still put the second-biggest objective damage on our side. Three deaths for a carry this involved is tidy, and all three came to Gideon, Iggy and Aurora. When one of those mages is unseen, Sparrow keeps Heightened Senses in reserve as her stealth exit before committing to a target.
perPlayer.3ac983bc-c000-403e-94c2-16bad9395206: Iggy & Scorch was their top damage and owned their only knockback, so Riktor's next job is simple: when Iggy sets up Inferno near our group, Riktor spends Riplash or Skewer on Iggy before peeling anyone else. The base is already built. Most wards on our team, most wards cleared, the most damage soaked on our side, a hand in close to half our kills and a clean early duo lane. Proper support work.
perPlayer.f8df0886-305c-4223-a0a0-d40b01e93bf1: No deaths, farm well above his usual, a big pile of healing and damage absorbed: Crunch built the safest offlane base on the board. Five assists across our 27 kills says the farm has not yet turned into team pressure on the scoreboard. When Wukong calls a Fangtooth or the team groups on a tower, Crunch shoves his wave first, then arrives with Right Crunch ready for the first enemy who reaches Belica or Sparrow.

12.4.call: Their Fangtooth fell in the same window as this teamfight, lost 2-3 with Wukong, Sparrow and Riktor dying. The timing does not show which came first.

19.2.call: Belica collected three kills in the same window as their Mini Prime, which fell with all five of us alive. Kill credits do not show who could reach the pit.

32.9.call: Belica and Wukong took two kills as their Inner Tower fell, and Orb Prime followed. The inhibitors and core went soon after. That is the finish to repeat: prize first, then the base.

matchup: Iggy & Scorch, Gideon and Aurora made three magical threats, with Iggy dealing their most damage.
Greystone was their sustain problem with the most healing in the lobby; Belica killed Gideon repeatedly.
build: Noxia needs a second, separate ability on the mark, so Seismic Assault into Void Bomb is the natural trigger.
Caustica gains damage against bonus magical armor, which suits Aurora's Flux Matrix and Frostguard.
Spellbreaker adds magical armor, and its spell shield raises her power while it holds.
eternal: Bottomless Vial pays only for River Buffs Belica personally kills, so team river control does not confirm her stacks.
Philosopher is the draft alternative for passive gold without the river requirement.
Keep this loadout while Belica can reach river buffs safely.
augment: Combat Veteran is a rotate-and-scale pick and the most common choice on Belica mid.
Nothing in this game shows another augment would have done more; keep Combat Veteran when rotations matter.
crest: Soulbearer's shield, magical lifesteal and movement speed defend against Gideon's and Iggy's magical burst, growing with Oblivion Crown.
Its use is not recorded, so the one death cannot be credited to it or blamed on it.
improvement: No swap is supported; this build is the standard to keep.
Greystone still died repeatedly, so a healing-reduction item was not needed.
If magical burst becomes the threat, Spellbreaker earlier gives up some damage for safety.

matchup: Greystone, the lobby's top healer, absorbed a huge amount of damage; Gideon, Murdock and Aurora were softer gank targets.
Gideon got two of Wukong's three deaths and Iggy & Scorch the other.
Three magical damage dealers are why the engine flags no magic resist on this build.
build: Tainted Trident is the direct answer to Greystone's sustain, and Infernum's burn grows against Draconum, Elafrost and Frostguard.
Mesmer's spell shield answers a single big spell but is not magical armor, so the flag stands.
eternal: Immaculate reduces damage only near full health, so it protects the opening of a fight, not the end.
Masterpiece is the draft alternative for kill-chaining; Prima Donna adds damage but makes him take more.
With deaths before both enemy Fangtooths, this game gives no reason to trade safety for damage.
augment: Masterful Mimicry brings clones more often in long fights and on objectives, fitting a Wukong who spent the game hitting objectives.
From Up High and Prosperous Path are the other options; keep Mimicry.
crest: Nex works as engage or chase, a dash that damages and slows nearby heroes.
Spending it to enter removes it as an exit, which matters when Gideon or Iggy can still hit him.
improvement: If Iggy's or Gideon's magic keeps landing first, magical armor trades some offense for survival; Mesmer already blocks one spell.
Keep Tainted Trident against a healing jungler like Greystone; it is Wukong's only anti-heal.

matchup: Aurora died three times and never killed Crunch.
Across their team, three magical damage sources were the threat to a melee diver, led by Iggy & Scorch.
Crunch was never killed, so the matchup did not punish the build; it does not show how often he reached their backline.
build: Crystalline Cuirass stacks magical armor while taking magical damage, a direct answer to three magical threats.
It leans more defensive than the common Augmentation, Mutilator and Salvation core; the deathless result fits but does not prove it.
eternal: Pilow weakens nearby enemies on each cast and Neurotoxin makes them take more damage, protecting and amplifying at once.
Pilow is the field's second choice, well behind Thraex, and its value depends on fighting close to several enemies.
Keep it when Crunch is the frontline the team fights around.
augment: Combo Crunch is the most-picked option by a distance and rewards long exchanges.
Lunge Crunch is a draft option if reaching the backline becomes the problem; nothing in this game shows that it was.
crest: Iceskorn Talons gives allies on its ice sheet physical power and movement speed while slowing enemies; Sparrow and Wukong benefit most.
improvement: No swap is supported by zero deaths with this much damage absorbed; keep the defensive shape.
If Crunch must finish their carry, Augmentation in place of Earthshaker trades some ability damage for faster empowered attacks.

matchup: Sparrow killed Murdock three times and Greystone four times.
Iggy was their top damage dealer and owned their only knockback, while Aurora's freeze added a stun.
The duo read came out ours: first Fangtooth went to us and only their duo died early.
build: Tainted Rounds is the direct tool against Greystone's healing, and Vanquisher executes heroes at a sliver of health.
Skipping Sky Splitter and Spectra from the common core did not visibly cost damage.
eternal: Weald's true-damage missiles on low-health heroes match a finisher's job alongside Vanquisher.
Taproot is the alternative if sustain in long trades becomes the problem, trading Wind-Rider's attack-speed burst for on-hit healing.
augment: Endless Hunt resets basic ability cooldowns on takedowns and adds penetration, scaling with this takedown-heavy game.
Sun Shards is the most-picked option; keep Endless Hunt while takedowns come this often.
crest: Eviscerator is a commitment tool, and its omnivamp helps her outlast Iggy's damage once committed.
Its use is not recorded, so neither her kills nor her deaths can be tied to it.
improvement: Keep the core; this game supports neither change.
If Iggy & Scorch keeps landing magical damage first, a defensive slot over Dust Devil trades attack speed for survival.
Against a jungler without heavy healing, Tainted Rounds becomes the slot to trade for raw damage such as Sky Splitter.

matchup: Iggy was their top damage dealer, magical, and owned their only knockback.
Greystone was the other sustained threat, and three magical sources are why the engine flags no magic resist.
build: Tainted Guard punishes Greystone or Murdock basic attacks with healing reduction and a bleed.
It is a durable physical-armor build with no magical armor, against a lobby whose top damage was magical.
eternal: Krix is the field's most common pick on Riktor support, and Cannibalism collects health from this many kills.
Festering Wounds is the alternative to Regenerative Tissue for anti-heal, giving up recovery between trades.
augment: Wanton Warden heals from damage taken, matching a game where Riktor absorbed more than anyone on our side.
Warden's Leash is the swap only if repositioning teammates becomes the main need. Keep it.
crest: Leafsong's Phantom Rush gives allies movement speed, slow immunity and passing through heroes, for a chase or an escape.
Its higher ward cap fits our top ward placer, and diminishing minion gold rewards staying off the waves.
improvement: A magical-armor item over Spectra or Gaia Greaves is the one change this lobby argues for: their top damage was magical.
It costs attack-based damage; keep Tainted Guard while Greystone and Murdock are basic-attacking him.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~0.5s of lockdown): Iggy & Scorch Inferno (knockback). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Crunch Right Crunch (knockup 1.25s), Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s), Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Riktor) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Forward Crunch gap-close stun → Right Crunch knockup → empowered Left Crunch, sustain via Re-Crunch
ourKits.winCondition: all-in a squishy with the empowered combo and heal back through Re-Crunch
ourKits.passive: post-ability empowered basic that refunds cooldowns
ourKits.playWith: peel-stripping engage so he reaches the backline
ourKits.playAgainst: peel/CC him off — without resets he's stranded; anti-heal blunts Re-Crunch

ourKits.combo: Windsurge engage → Cyclebreaker damage-reduction spin → clones from 84000 Hairs
ourKits.winCondition: stance-dance for damage or tankiness and overwhelm with clones
ourKits.playWith: a team that fights alongside his clones
ourKits.playAgainst: AoE clears his clones; CC him during the damage-reduction window

ourKits.combo: Riplash pull → Shock Therapy silence → Skewer suppress ult
ourKits.winCondition: pull a target in and chain silence+suppress for a guaranteed kill
ourKits.playWith: burst that deletes his pulled/suppressed target
ourKits.playAgainst: respect Riplash range — stay spaced; cleanse/QSS the suppress

ourKits.combo: Seismic Assault knockup → Void Bomb → Neural Disruptor silence ult, Void Drone mana drain
ourKits.winCondition: knock up + silence a target and burst with missing-HP scaling
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Seismic Assault; she's immobile — dive when ult is down

ourKits.combo: Piercing Shot poke → Heightened Senses AS → Hail of Arrows zone → Inner Fire ult
ourKits.winCondition: ramp Relentless + AS and sustained-DPS the front down
ourKits.playWith: heavy peel — she's immobile and pure DPS
ourKits.playAgainst: she has zero escape — hard-engage her and she dies first

enemyKits.combo: Oil Spill → Molotov ignite → Flame Turret → Inferno knockback ult
enemyKits.winCondition: layer fire zones on a choke/objective and burn the team
enemyKits.playWith: CC that holds enemies in his fire
enemyKits.playAgainst: don't fight in his zones — flank; kill the turret, dive him

enemyKits.combo: Boreal Sweep slow → Hoarfrost root → Glacial Charge engage → Cryoseism stun ult
enemyKits.winCondition: chain frost CC (slow→root→stun) to lock the fight down
enemyKits.playWith: burst that converts her long CC chain into kills
enemyKits.playAgainst: she's a CC battery — cleanse/QSS the Cryoseism stun; spread to avoid the chain

enemyKits.combo: Void Breach slow → Cosmic Rift → Black Hole on the grouped enemies
enemyKits.winCondition: land Black Hole / Cosmic Rift on a clumped team for AoE burst
enemyKits.passive: an ability-empowered basic tethers a target for bonus damage
enemyKits.playWith: hard engage that clumps enemies into his Black Hole
enemyKits.playAgainst: immobile with long cooldowns — dodge the skillshots and dive him once Black Hole is down

enemyKits.combo: Static Trap root → Buckshot → Hot Pursuit AS → Long Arm of the Law global snipe
enemyKits.winCondition: trap for the root, then out-range with Shots Fired and finish with the global ult
enemyKits.passive: every 5th basic is a long-range bonus shot
enemyKits.playWith: frontline/peel to protect his low mobility
enemyKits.playAgainst: almost no escape — engage past the trap and he dies

enemyKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap → Make Way armor shred → Sacred Oath empowered basic → Stone Forged Soul stasis ult
enemyKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
enemyKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
enemyKits.playAgainst: don't waste burst into his stasis — wait it out; anti-heal cuts the ult heal

riktor.loadout: Krix (Regenerative Tissue + Cannibalism), augment Wanton Warden, crest Leafsong
fedBy: Cannibalism (minor): Takedowns permanently increase your Maximum Health by 25.
lines: Lead story: Hard to kill. Died 2 times in 37 minutes, fewer deaths than about 87% of Riktor support players this patch. The build added health and armor and healing off damage.
Skewer at rank 3: 85s base, about 59.4s by the end (30% shorter) from 43 ability haste: Tainted Guard 8, Elafrost 15, Gaia Greaves 10, Spectra 10.
12 takedowns (1 kills, 11 assists) fed: Cannibalism (minor).
Riktor dealt 12,883 hero damage, 8% of their team's, with +0 magical power from items.
Tainted Guard (item): On being hit by a Basic Attack: Reduce the Source's Healing by 45% for 3s. Apply a Bleed dealing 30 (+30%) Damage over 3s.
Elafrost (item): On Ability Cast: Empower your next Basic Attack within 4s. Deal 70 (+2%) Damage On-Hit around the Target. Slows by 35% for 1.5s. Damage is increased by 60% against Monsters.
Gaia Greaves (item): Move to generate up to 100 stacks: Stacks grant up to 40 Movement Speed. Basic Attacks expend all stacks for bonus Damage. Deals up to 40 (+60%)(+5%) Damage.
Overlord (item): On Successful Basic Attack: Deal (+1%) Damage. Deal (+30%) (+2.5%) Damage around the Target. Damage decreases from 100% to 50% based on distance.
Wanton Warden (augment): Regenerate Health equal to 4-7% of damage taken over 5s. Increases with Hero Level.
Sustain: Tainted Guard: On being hit by a Basic Attack: Reduce the Source's Healing by 45% for 3s. Apply a Bleed dealing 30 (+30%) Damage over 3s.; 11,442 healing recorded.
Toughness: +1270 health, +150 physical armor; took 44,980 damage, mitigated 54,006, died 2 times.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 5 effects on one trigger: Tainted Guard, Elafrost, Gaia Greaves, Spectra, Overlord.
Countered? 0 of the 1 players Riktor killed built magical armor. Anti-heal on Iggy & Scorch, Gideon, Greystone. We killed Riktor 2 times.
Copy it? Krix (Regenerative Tissue + Cannibalism): 49.7% in 3,895 Riktor support games, level with the hero's 50.5%. A standard setup: what made it work was this game, not a secret build.

card.lesson: Skewer came back about every 59s instead of 85s by the end (30% shorter). Count it, and take fights while it is down.

lt-belica.loadout: Aion (Bottomless Vial + Runic Focus), augment Combat Veteran, crest Soulbearer
lines: Lead story: Damage well above normal. 1,590 hero damage a minute, more than 98% of Lt. Belica mid players this patch (38% of the team's). Penetration did the work: Gideon took about 33% more magical damage than their armor allowed (estimate).
Neural Disruptor at rank 3: 85s base, about 61.6s by the end (28% shorter) from 38 ability haste: Noxia 20, Spellbreaker 10, Soulbearer 8.
Lt. Belica dealt 58,841 hero damage, 38% of their team's, with +575 magical power from items.

Penetration: Combustion 9, Wraith Leggings 11, Caustica ignores 35%; against Gideon (level 17: about 47 magical armor, 11 after penetration; took 23,259 magical damage from heroes, 67% of all hero damage they took) and Iggy & Scorch (level 18: about 49 magical armor, 12 after penetration; took 14,219 magical damage from heroes, 65% of all hero damage they took) that is about 33% and 33% more damage (estimate: percent penetration taken before flat).
Combustion (item): On dealing Ability Damage: Deal 50 (+18%) Damage to the Target and nearby Enemies.
Noxia (item): Deal 6% of Target's Maximum Health as bonus Damage.
Wraith Leggings (item): Against Heroes below 40% Health: Abilities deal 12% bonus Magical Damage.
Caustica (item): On dealing Ability Damage to a Hero: While they are above 50% Health. For every point of Bonus Magical Armor they possess. Deal 0.2% more Damage.
Aion (Eternal): Casting a spell grants 1 Mana Regeneration for 8s (stacks 5x). Spells also grant gold equal to 6% of damage dealt to Enemy Heroes.
